newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Feeds group Nutreco plans Amsterdam share listing.
newsitem.headline: Feeds group Nutreco plans Amsterdam share listing.

text.p: Dutch animal and fish feeds group Nutreco Holding, which has global sales of more than four billion guilders a year, said on Monday it planned a listing on the Amsterdam stock market by the end of the summer.

Chief Executive Officer Richard van Wijnbergen said an initial public offering would give Nutreco access to a larger capital market, facilitate any future acquisitions and boost the company's international reputation.
"We think the Dutch financial market is in good shape, Nutreco is in good shape, so it's a good time to go to the market," he said at a press briefing.
Nutreco also unveiled full-year 1996 profits of 40.4 million guilders, up more than 50 percent from 1995's 26.0 million. Turnover was up more than 13 percent to 4.56 billion guilders.
Operating income rose 13.3 percent to 128 million guilders and Nutreco said it expected 1997 operating results to show a further improvement if current market conditions persisted.
"There are attractions in the company particularly, in aquaculture, this is where we expect to see good growth," said one Dutch analyst who declined to be named.
The company has leading positions in animal and fish feed markets around the world and employs some 5,500 people in 60 locations in 15 countries.

It is split into two divisions -- agriculture and aquaculture with agriculture accounting for almost 80 percent of turnover. The fish feeds division controls some 40 percent of the world fish feeds market.
In January Nutreco expanded its Japanese operations through a joint venture with Yamaha Motor Corp, making Yamaha Nutreco's exclusive sales partner for farmed fish in Japan.

Nutreco emerged in 1994 from a $425 million management buyout of British Petroleum's nutrition unit, much of which was based in the Netherlands, and has since has concentrated on restructuring its financial base.
Last year it privately placed cumulative preference shares with five Dutch financial inititutions, raising 150 million guilders to reduce its long-term debt.

These institutions -- Fortis Amev, ING's Nationale-Nederlanden, NIB, Rabobank and ABM AMRO -- will continue to hold a stake in Nutreco after the listing, Chief Financial Officer Peter Paul Verhallen said.

"The share issue is completely separate," he said, adding discussions were continuing with the global co-ordinators of the deal, Goldman Sachs International and Rabo Secutities, and it was too early to estimate the size of the offering.

Chief executive Van Wijnbergen said Nutreco had felt an impact from the outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands but its international and multi-sector exposure had limited any damage. Nutreco derives 75 to 80 percent of its turnover from outside the Netherlands.
"I would be very surprised if the Dutch results were not lower but this will be compensated by revenue rises elsewhere," he said.
